subject.title: [Bug]: TLS certificate pin mismatch loop when connecting through Cloudflare Tunnel/Access (anycast edge certs)

question: For iOS Remote Domain connections through publicly trusted reverse proxies, should gateway identity move from one TLS leaf pin to the paired gateway's stable application identity, or should the app retain a bounded multi-pin TOFU policy?
rationale: Both viable fixes alter the security contract: CA-only transport validation requires a separate authenticated gateway identity, while multi-pin TOFU expands and manages the set of certificates accepted for an endpoint.

options.title: Bind gateway identity
options.body: Use platform CA validation for public WSS and verify the stable identity established during gateway pairing on every connection.

options.title: Bounded multi-pin TOFU
options.body: Persist a small user-approved pin set with explicit replacement, expiry, and removal semantics for rotating or anycast endpoints.

options.title: Keep single-leaf pinning
options.body: Preserve the current security boundary and explicitly document Cloudflare-style anycast Remote Domain endpoints as unsupported.

recommendation.title: Bind gateway identity
recommendation.body: Use platform CA validation for public WSS and verify the stable identity established during gateway pairing on every connection.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history is most directly associated with the iOS security stack and mandatory TLS policy surrounding this choice.
